messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@acmecorp.com>, James Miller <jmiller@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Acme MAP: mutual action plan recap

Hi Sofia / James —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to keep momentum. I captured the key pain points and suggested owners / dates below. Please flag anything I missed. I attached the MAP (redwood-MAP-v1.2.pdf) with a one-page summary and milestones.

Attendees (today):
- Sofia Lopez (Head of ML)
- James Miller (CTO)
- Lena Park (Procurement)
- Marissa Cole (Redwood, Solutions)
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood, Sales)
- Connor O'Brien (Redwood, CS)

Key pain points / goals:
- Performance variability on large-context prompts causing latency spikes during peak loads — goal: 99th percentile latency < 300ms for the critical endpoint.
- Unit cost per 1k tokens is higher than ideal — goal: reduce inference cost by 30% through batching/quantization.
- Data residency & auditability: some workloads must remain in-region and have detailed audit logs (SOC2 + exportable logs).
- Proof-of-value: need a short POC with representative dataset and throughput targets to validate performance and cost.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Technical deep dive & infra checklist — Mar 24, 2027 — Owner: Marissa / Connor — objective: validate integration approach, VPC/KMS requirements, and sequence length distribution.
2) POC environment & baseline run — Apr 4–Apr 18, 2027 — Owner: Acme engineering (Sofia/Jim) + Redwood infra — objective: run 1-week baseline at target throughput and capture latency/cost.
3) Cost/quantization tuning & optimization — Apr 19–May 2, 2027 — Owner: Redwood runtime team (Rishi + Marissa) — objective: demonstrate target cost reduction with quantization/batching.
4) Procurement & legal review — May 3–May 17, 2027 — Owner: Acme procurement (Lena) + Redwood legal — objective: finalize T&Cs and SLA.
5) Exec review & decision — May 20, 2027 — Owner: James (CTO) + Redwood leadership — objective: go/no-go.

Decision process / stakeholders:
- Technical signoff: Sofia (ML lead) + James (CTO)
- Procurement & contract signoff: Lena Park
- Exec signoff: James (CTO)

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa: send MAP doc (attached) and HubSpot deal link — sent.
- Sofia: confirm availability for Mar 24 technical deep dive.
- Rishi: will share initial pricing template and DocuSign route after technical validation.

Attachments: redwood-MAP-v1.2.pdf (one-page summary + milestone table)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2027-01

If that all looks right I’ll lock the technical deep dive for Mar 24 at 10:00am PT.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Timeline: the exec review we mentioned is likely May 20, but procurement may need an extra week for final signatures if there are contract tweaks (so May 27 is our conservative finish).
- POC scope: can we limit the first run to 3 representative models / prompt families and a 1-hour steady-state load to capture tail latency? That will let us evaluate both latency and cost quickly.
- SOC2 evidence: procurement will want SOC2 and data-handling evidence up-front. Can you point us to the SOC2 report and typical audit logs?

I’m available for the Mar 24 technical deep dive (10:00am PT works). Please send calendar invite with a short agenda (integration endpoints, VPC/KMS, sequence length distributions).

Thanks,
Sofia
